title: A normal installed-build update must not block cross-host mailbox or direct prompts: peers re-attest compatibility automatically instead of needing a manual pinned-profile refresh
outcome: After a routine build update on either host of an enrolled pair, ordinary cross-host mailbox delivery and direct prompts keep working with no operator ceremony. Either the peer re-attests and refreshes its compatibility record automatically and safely, or delivery continues on an unchanged protocol/schema/key basis. Build hashes stay as diagnostic and attestation evidence only, never as delivery authority.
acceptance: The code path that pins a peer's compatibility to a binary-hash profile and refuses or holds ordinary delivery when it changes is identified in a note, with file and line, together with the safety property the pin is meant to protect.

With the fix, deterministic tests show that after either peer's binary hash changes with the federation protocol/schema contract and keys unchanged, ordinary mailbox send, read and ack and direct-prompt delivery succeed with no manual profile refresh; that an already enrolled pair with stored profile schema '2' reconnects after both hosts restart with the '2-metadata-units-2' local storage layout and unchanged federation contract, without profile rewriting or re-enrollment; that a change in the federation protocol/schema contract or keys is still refused or re-attested safely; and that the build hash remains recorded as diagnostic or attestation evidence. Local storage compatibility and migration checks remain enforced independently.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope finding of Medium or higher.

completion.summary: Historical delivered work reconciled; 00a4ecea; R9 compatibility tests/pair and landing provenance; reconcile final gate/criterion links. Later link incidents are not proof build-hash pinning persists; live child separate.
